Satellites measure how green your maize is. Green, strong maize gives a high number. Weak or dry maize gives a low number.\n\nWe compare your plot with what is normal for maize planted on the same day. If your plot stays below normal for more than one satellite pass, we tell you.
Confidence shows how sure the system is. Clouds and missing pictures lower it.\n\nWhen confidence is low, a person checks the result. A plot is never judged on missing data.
A covered plot is insured for the season. If satellites see a big loss, a claim starts by itself.\n\nYour cooperative or insurer adds plots to the cover. You do not pay in the app.
How is the harvest forecast made?
We add up how green your maize has been this season and compare it with past seasons on the same plot.\n\nIt is an early prototype and a wide range. It is not a promise about your harvest.

1. Satellites watch every covered plot.
2. If the loss passes the agreed level, a claim starts by itself. You do not need to fill a form.
3. An insurance officer checks the evidence. An agent may visit.
4. If approved, the payout goes to your mobile money (simulated here).

You can ask for a review once for each decision.

1. Add your maize plot: type its UPI, add your e-title, and walk around its edge with your phone.
2. Your cooperative agent checks the plot.
3. Satellites check your maize once a week.
4. If your maize looks weak, you get an alert.
5. If a covered plot loses too much, a claim starts by itself and a person decides it.
Why does the planting date matter?
Maize grows differently each week. We compare your plot with normal maize of the same age, so the planting date must be right.\n\nYour cooperative agent can correct it.

1. Go to one corner of the plot.
2. Wait until the GPS is ready, then tap "I'm at this corner".
3. Walk along the edge to the next corner and tap again.
4. Do this for every corner, in order, all the way round.
5. Tap "Finish the walk". Rinda draws the boundary from the corners you walked.
